To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shell-model plus Hartree- Fock calculations for the Ca isotopes reproduce the experimental binding energies, the single-particle spectra, the B(E2) values for the 2+ states, the quadrupole deformation, and the magnetic moments of the ground states.

(1) the shell model is the most successful and accurate model for nuclear structure calculations and (2) the shell model can now be applied to nuclei with up to 20 nucleons in the valence space and with up to 10 valence nucleons.
the shell model plus Hartree-Foc calculations for the neutron- rich Ca isotopes are able to reproduce the experimental data for the binding energies, charge radii and magnetic moments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear shell-model in the context of a realistic nucleon-nucleon potential and the inclusion of a mean field to account for the long-range part of the nucleon-nucleus interaction.
the structure and reactions of nuclei far from stability and with the structure of nuclei near stability as determined by the structure of the nuclei far from stability.
the evolution of collective nuclear properties as a function of particle number.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shell-model plus HF approach has been very successful in describing nuclear structure properties in the sd shell.
the shell-model plus Hartree- Fock approach has been very successful in describing the properties of the Ca isotopes.

a shell-model calculation of the Ca isotopes with the same interaction as used for the O isotopes reproduces the data quite well, and that the shell-model plus Hartree- Fock calculation reproduces the data even better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to calculate nuclear structure properties of neutron-rich Ca isotopic chain.
we have developed a method to describe the properties of the nuclei near the doubly-magic nuclei 40 Ca and 48 Ca.
we have developed a new method to calculate the shell-model matrix elements and the Hartree-Fock potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of the neutron-rich Ca region are determined by the single-particle structure and that the shell-model description of the region is quite satisfactory.
the shell model plus Hartree-Foc calculations can reproduce the properties of the neutron-rich calcium isotopes.
a spherical shell-model description is sufficient for describing the structure of the Ca isotopes up to 44Ca.
